scope: Local macOS arm64 cumulative engine builds and file-only inline DAQ verdict/forwarded-byte comparisons. No live interface, installation or deployment.
changes: Ignore timestamps that were not negotiated, including zero-valued late options.
Retain negotiated protection for zero clocks and apply wrap-aware ordering without the Linux one-tick tolerance.
Preserve normalization policy and data/ACK sequence boundaries when opening SYN or SYN-ACK packets contain data.
Use existing native events 129:4 and 129:14; no new signature or production configuration change.

baseline.scope: File-only inline DAQ verdicts and forwarded bytes. No live interface or deployed routing.

replay.scope: File-only inline DAQ verdicts and forwarded bytes. No live interface or deployed routing.

sanitized_replay.scope: File-only inline DAQ verdicts and forwarded bytes. No live interface or deployed routing.

regular.scope: Build and pure-parser checks only. Load and PCAP replay must be validated separately.

sanitized.scope: Address/undefined-instrumented protocol plugin; unchanged instrumented perimeter library; separately built AddressSanitizer engine.

profiles.scope: Native configuration loading and effective rule states only; no traffic or live inline enforcement.

dns_profiles.scope: Configuration and effective rule states only; not packet forwarding or deployment.

metadata.scope: Synthetic inline file replay only. SID 9202999 is a fixture-only drop of valid handshake offers; it is not part of the deployed ruleset.
Synthetic file-only inline DAQ verdicts and forwarded packet bytes; no live interface or deployment.
Actual file-only inline DAQ verdicts and output bytes for existing fixtures; no live deployment.

configuration.scope: Native configuration loading and effective rule states only; no traffic or live inline enforcement.

metadata.source_route_decode_guard: Three malformed IPv4 source routes now raise native IPv4-option event 116:4 from the UDP decoder as well as rule 9201012. Both events, required rejection and zero checksum-failure counters are checked.

metadata.scope: Synthetic file-only inline dump:pcap DAQ verdicts and forwarded bytes; no deployed sandbox or live interface.

profiles.scope: Configuration and effective rule states only; not packet forwarding or deployment.

limitations: The agent source networks require anti-spoofing and an unavoidable host network boundary.
Inbound control traffic requires trusted router and connection-state policy outside these signatures.
The DNS proxy rejects encrypted or unauthorized application data at its allowed socket; these rules constrain routing only.
Blocked fragment captures may forward an orphan fragment; the complete denied datagram must never reach the endpoint.
HTTP content policy and actual DNS application behavior have separate tests; this is finite network fixture coverage.

metadata.scope: File-only inline DAQ verdicts and forwarded bytes. No live endpoint, Mobile IPv6 binding state or deployed route is tested.
metadata.comparison: Same engine and plugins; reconstructed previous configuration removes only Home Address boundary SID 9202016 and its enabled state.

configuration.scope: Configuration and effective rule states only; not packet forwarding or deployment.

limitations: Opaque protocol sweep uses empty and zero-filled payloads; it is not semantic conformance for 254 other protocols.
Encapsulation coverage is bounded to IP-in-IP and plain GRE with IPv4/IPv6 TCP/UDP inner controls.
Home Address rejection is fixed-peer local policy. General protocol validation and authenticated Mobile IPv6 support are separate concerns.
The comparison confirms forwarding changed at the sensor; it does not demonstrate successful application impersonation on a live host.
Each report case counts once even when two comparison configurations were exercised.

historical_findings_not_added_again.interpretation: Initial 2688-case fixtures incorrectly padded Timestamp before Fast Open, leaving nonzero bytes after EOL. Superseded.
Corrected 2688-case baseline before expansion; superseded by the final matched baseline.
One-file timestamp prototype left 144 failures caused by SYN-data handshake downgrading.
Instrumented repetition of the one-file prototype, with the same 144 failures.
Expanded intermediate baseline used a syn-data label that accidentally selected fragmentation. Superseded by opening-data fixtures.
Three-file prototype left 60 stale-timestamp failures after opening data; intermediate syn-data label also selected fragmentation.
Instrumented repetition of the three-file prototype, with the same 60 failures and intermediate fixture label.

evidence_correction: The first cumulative report recursively scanned the macOS dSYM sidecar named ax_nd_options.so, overwriting the library basename with the debug-symbol hash. The verified cumulative run uses a separate directory containing only byte-identical loaded libraries, and its hashes match the timestamp sanitizer run. Both reports are retained; the repeated 241 cases are counted zero additional times.
limitations: This is selected timestamp and SYN-data behavior, not complete TCP/RFC conformance or authentication of timestamp values and Fast Open cookies.
Native stream bookkeeping is not proved to commit only after final DAQ admission. The separate SACK guard has its own narrower admission-state contract.

Timestamp echo behavior, long-idle aging and every serial-arithmetic boundary remain unproved. The comparator conservatively denies an exactly half-range difference; this corpus does not separately test that ambiguous boundary.
The full engine uses AddressSanitizer; the protocol plugin additionally uses UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. Whole-engine UBSan coverage is not asserted.

Only 3120 new final packet case checks enter the combined inventory. Baselines, corrected/prototype corpora, probes, diagnostic builds, 3120 sanitizer repetitions, 3884 existing regressions and the additional 241-case evidence correction are excluded.
Historical evidence retains its original source hashes. Passing reports here do not imply that every historical suite was rerun against this engine.
Linux runtime behavior, deployed sandbox routing, universal RFC/W3C compliance and prevention of every unknown attack remain unproved.
